title: Startup probe delete silently swallowed on error
description: In all four backend startup_probe functions (transit/azure_store.rs:101, transit/gcs_store.rs:93, reader/post/azure_store.rs:95, reader/post/gcs_store.rs:87), the probe DELETE uses 'let _ = store.delete(&probe).await' — the error is discarded. If the DELETE fails (e.g. due to an IAM policy that grants PutObject but not DeleteObject, or a transient error), the probe object '_stoa_write_probe' lingers in the container/bucket permanently. On next startup, the PUT will succeed again (idempotent), so this does not prevent startup, but the leftover object is invisible to the operator. More importantly: if the DELETE fails silently, the probe has not confirmed delete permission, which is part of what the probe is supposed to verify for the GC path. This is the same pattern that existed in s3_store.rs before this commit (inherited comment 'best-effort; harmless if it lingers') — but it was never correct. A probe that does not confirm delete permission cannot assure the GC code will work.
